summary: Caroline A. F. Rhys Davids worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at University College London and under Thomas William Rhys Davids, later lecturing at the University of Manchester and SOAS, and serving as President of the Pali Text Society.

Caroline Humphrey is a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. Educated at Girton College, Cambridge, and under Edmund Leach, she held positions at the University of Cambridge, King's College, Scott Polar Research Institute, and University of Michigan.

Carolyn Patricia Shields is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her Master of Arts at Indiana University by 1998, studying under Christopher I. Beckwith, György Kara, Larry Moses, and Michael L. Walter.

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, later serving as a Graduate Teaching Associate there and as a Visiting Lecturer at Denison University.
Carson Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. In 1997, he took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Catherine Bell specialized in religious studies and sinology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Joseph Mitsuo Kitagawa and served from 1985 to 2008 as the Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University.

Catherine Elaine Prueitt works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied at the University of Rochester and Emory University, where she completed her PhD under John D. Dunne, Laurie L. Patton, Sara L. McClintock, Vincent J. Cornell, and Isabelle Ratié.

Catherine Ludvik specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto under David Waterhouse and others, and held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Hanazono University.
Cathy Cantwell works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Kent by 1989 and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge and Oxford under Edward Byles Cowell and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and Cambridge, serving as Professor of Sanskrit.

Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University. He held academic posts at Yale University, the University of Chicago, and the University of Virginia, where he served as Professor of English from around 1970 to 1991.
Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Delog Dawa Drolma, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Dudjom Rinpoche, and later taught Albion Moonlight Butters.

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He conducted research at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and served as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago from around 2006 to 2021.

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. After earning his doctorate at the University of Oxford, he held posts at Trinity College, Oxford, the National University of Singapore, Clare Hall, Cambridge, and Lancaster University.

Chamnong Adivadhanasit works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA at Chulalongkorn University, where he later worked as a part-time instructor, and served as a Professor in the Faculty of Social Science at Kasetsart University.

Chandrabhal Tripathi was an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held academic positions at Göttingen, Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Cologne, and the Free University of Berlin.

Chang-geun Hwang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000. During his studies, he was supervised by Morten Schlütter and worked with Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Gudrun Bühnemann.

Changhwan Park is a professor at Geumgang University specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University and earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt, Padmanabh S. Jaini, Robert H. Sharf, and George L. Hart.

Changpei Luo was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Peking University from 1916 to 1921. He subsequently held posts at Northwest University, Xiamen University, Sun Yat-sen University, and Peking University.

Chanju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he completed his PhD under the supervision of Minoru Kiyota, Charles Hallisey, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda.
